cells.tense: The form is finished and still holding, and you are here for it.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Pick the piece of this upkeep only your hands can do, and carry that piece whole rather than splitting it thin or handing it off. Keep it up through the ordinary stretches where nobody is checking whether it holds.
cells.core:
Something you steered for a long time is standing now, and the read on what matters arrives before any argument for it does. That's why the upkeep lands where it counts instead of everywhere at once, and why the whole thing holds without being gripped.

What's yours to grow is stamina. There's a share of this work that no one else can take, and the weight in it is ordinary and real. Carry that share complete instead of spreading it thin. The middle stretch of it will feel plain, and plain is fine — a thing that stands doesn't need you to make it stand again every morning. It needs you to keep picking up your end.

cells.verb: bringing a long effort through to something that stands

cells.tense: You are bracing for a finish line that hasn't been drawn yet.
cells.act: sit somewhere new with nothing in your hands and let whatever comes, come
cells.ask: Find a spot you'd usually pass by — a bench, a step, a different room — and sit there twenty minutes with your hands empty. Whatever shows up, including the jitter, is allowed to show up.
cells.core:
You've been steering past the point where this was finished — more established, further out, a next stage arriving in the head before today's work is set down. Attention that once said what mattered has narrowed into checking every part at once, bracing for a verdict nobody has given yet.

What opens this back up begins empty. Sit somewhere with no task in your hands for twenty minutes and let whatever shows up show up, the jitter included, without sorting it into useful or wasted. Sitting there with no plan is the difficult part, not a step toward the next thing. Something can arrive whole only into a space you haven't already filled.

cells.tense: You brought something all the way through, and then stopped counting yourself in it.
cells.act: describe what is in front of your eyes in five plain lines, no conclusions
cells.ask: Write five plain lines about what's nearest — desk, street, sink — with no conclusion drawn. Read them back once, then put them away.
cells.core:
The effort you carried through is somewhere in the shape of your days, and the part of you that once aimed it went quiet. You did the doing and set aside what you were reaching for, and the whole arc isn't in the frame anymore. What you carried through was real; the aim you held while carrying it fell out of the account.

Clear seeing doesn't come back in one piece — it comes back as a first glance. Write five lines about what's nearest you and stop at five, meaning attached to none of them. That's the whole act. Glance at the lines once, then put them away. Looking at a thing as if you'd just arrived is how the aim gets found again, and you find it by standing near it.
cells.sheetLine: What you carried through still stands. It stopped being yours in your own account.
cells.verb: bringing a long effort through to something that stands

cells.tense: You are writing the story of what happens next and calling it someone else's plan.
cells.act: notice what is before your eyes before naming it
cells.ask: Once this week, when a message or offer arrives, take in what it plainly says before you decide what it's really about. A minute of that first is enough.
cells.core:
There's a hand on the tiller here, and in your telling the tiller steers itself. The next stage came together by accident, the calls went a certain way, the openings belonged to somebody else. The structure keeps rising because you keep aiming your attention where it counts, and the aiming is the part you leave out of the account.

Take one plain fact before the story lands on it — what was actually written, what was actually offered — and let that fact sit alone for a minute. No credit to claim, nothing to announce. You're only staying with what's there while it happens, and staying with it is what makes it yours.
cells.sheetLine: Something is steering toward the next stage. Luck is your name for it.
